name: Comic Book Art
visualIdentity: Explicitly described as comic book art: panel layouts, bold contours, exaggerated poses, speed lines and purposeful sound effect lettering. Choose one coherent drawing and printing language; preserve accurate, readable dialogue.
suitableUses: Best for narrative panels, expressive character action, explainers and action titles. It can carry accurate charts or maps inside inked panels. These are inferred uses supported by the style guidance.
limitations: Avoid mixing conflicting comic traditions, obscuring dialogue, distorting data or using speed lines on static values. Gaze motion requires suitable eyes and layers or a rig. Omit it if it distorts the face or distracts. Energetic opening motion may not suit restrained topics.
palette: The suggested five discrete tokens are background #FFF2D9, foreground #1C2230, and accents #C9403C, #E1B744 and #3768A1. They are optional for new art only; exact task, brand, reference and existing asset colors take precedence. No gradients are enabled. The red accent with background misses the stated 4.5 text contrast target; use it decoratively, not for body text. Check actual composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Separate panels, characters, lettering and masks; use real text and key pose changes to set reading rhythm. Stage entrances, speed lines and bounded impact pops with readable holds. For video, derive every state from seekable composition time; scroll, hover and pointer input apply only to interactive delivery. Motion recipes are optional and must fit the scene.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience or silence for the topic and user requirements. Sound effects may emphasize action, but are not mandatory. Keep dialogue intelligible, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and check sync in the delivered video.
assetRequirements: Separate layered artwork or numbered frames with transparency, consistent dimensions and clear naming. Preserve authored transforms and exact copy; inspect assets before composition. Optional Rough.js can make seeded sketch contours or hachure, but does not provide handwriting, authentic print materials, poses or animation.
combinations: Use alone for panels and character action. Pair with style-097 when accurate charts or maps belong inside panels, retaining data integrity and the limited palette; or style-093 for timed sound effect and title lettering. Keep dialogue readable and avoid conflicting lettering traditions.
productionApproach: Select visual and motion tools by fidelity and scene needs; SVG is suited to scalable panels, strokes and masks, while PixiJS can composite many 2D sprites. GSAP is the primary seekable timeline option; optional Motion needs explicit synchronization. HyperFrames owns composition, timing, sync, validation and export. Use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, and record why. Inspect representative frames and the decoded result.
